hints: A normal letter in the pattern allows exactly one next letter, but a . allows any. How would you handle "any" if words were stored letter by letter in a tree?

Store words in a trie with an end-of-word flag. Search with DFS/backtracking: on a letter follow that single child, on a dot try every existing child, and succeed only if you finish the pattern on a node marked as a word end.

1. addWord: normal trie insert, mark the last node as end.
  2. search(pattern) calls dfs(root, 0).
  3. If i == pattern length, return node.isEnd.
  4. If pattern[i] is a letter: go to that child (fail if missing) and recurse with i+1.
  5. If it is a dot: for every non-null child, if dfs(child, i+1) is true return true; otherwise return false.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Keep a list of words; for each search compare the pattern against every word of the same length, treating dots as matches.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Trie + DFS: letters follow one branch; only dots fan out, and the constraints keep dots few.
approaches.time: O(L) per add; O(L) per search without dots, up to O(26^d·L) with d dots

explain: Sample: after adding cake and coke, the root has child c which branches into a and o. For c.ke we follow c, then the dot tries both a and o; the a branch continues k→e and lands on a flagged node, so the answer is true. cak ends on the k node whose flag is false, so it is false (length must match). ...e fans out three times but finds cake; b... fails at once because root has no b child. Edge case: always check the end flag, not just that the path exists.
recognize: 'Store words, then match patterns where a dot means any letter' → trie plus DFS that branches only on the wildcard.
